title: Meta Quest 3S Review: The New King of Budget VR?
subtitle: Meta's latest headset brings Quest 3 power to a much more accessible price point.
author: Technova Team
content:
The Meta Quest 3S has arrived, promising to democratize high-end mixed reality. By stripping away some of the premium flourishes of the standard Quest 3 while keeping the core processing power, Meta has created a compelling entry point for VR newcomers and upgraders alike.

The Quest 3S delivers a high-quality VR experience without the flagship price tag.

Performance: No Compromises on Power

Under the hood, the Quest 3S is powered by the same Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 chipset found in its more expensive sibling. Paired with 8GB of RAM, this means the 3S can run every game and application in the Quest library with the same performance as the flagship model. Loading times are snappy, and complex mixed reality experiences run without a hitch.

Display and Optics: The Trade-off

To hit the lower price point, Meta opted for Fresnel lenses instead of the pancake optics found on the Quest 3. The resolution stands at 1832x1920 per eye. While you lose some of the edge-to-edge clarity and the slim profile of the pancake lenses, the visual experience remains sharp enough for most gaming and media consumption. The 4MP RGB passthrough cameras ensure that mixed reality remains a core part of the experience, offering full-color views of your surroundings.

Design and Comfort

The headset is slightly bulkier than the Quest 3 due to the lens assembly, but it remains comfortable for extended sessions. It uses the same Touch Plus controllers, which lack the tracking rings of older models, making them much more ergonomic and less prone to clashing during intense gameplay.
